feed.title: Pronounce — recent dictionary additions
feed.subtitle: How engineers actually pronounce project / product / jargon names. Community-maintained.

entry.title: musl — muscle
entry.summary: musl is pronounced "muscle" (/ˈmʌsəl/). Lightweight libc behind Alpine Linux images; official site says "musl, pronounced like the word 'mussel' or 'muscle'".

entry.title: axios — ak see ose
entry.summary: axios is pronounced "ak see ose" (/ˈæksioʊs/). Promise-based HTTP client among npm's most-downloaded packages; from Greek axios ("worthy") with no official ruling — top-voted community reading is "AK-see-ohs".

entry.title: Mockito — mah kee toh
entry.summary: Mockito is pronounced "mah kee toh" (/mɑːˈkiːtoʊ/). Java mocking framework whose name is a maintainer-confirmed pun on mock + mojito; a maintainer answered issue #889 with mock-based /mɑˈkiːtoʊ/ ("mah-KEE-toh"), while creator Szczepan Faber told the mailing list to "go ahead and pronounce it the mojito way" ("moh-KEE-toh"), so the split is genuine.

entry.title: xonsh — kahnsh
entry.summary: xonsh is pronounced "kahnsh" (/kɑːnʃ/). Python-powered cross-platform shell; the official homepage states it "sounds like 'consh'".

entry.title: Pyodide — pie uh dyed
entry.summary: Pyodide is pronounced "pie uh dyed" (/ˈpaɪəˌdaɪd/). CPython compiled to WebAssembly for running Python in the browser; maintainers rth and hoodmane gave the IPA ˈpɑɪ.ə.ˌdɑɪd (Py + Iodide — rhymes with iodide).

entry.title: Haxe — hex
entry.summary: Haxe is pronounced "hex" (/hɛks/). Cross-platform language compiling to JS, C++, JVM and more; early official docs said "hex" while English speakers naturally say "hacks" — no creator ruling, both survive at conferences.

entry.title: FLTK — full tick
entry.summary: FLTK is pronounced "full tick" (/ˈfʊltɪk/). Veteran cross-platform C++ GUI toolkit; the official docs open with 'The Fast Light Tool Kit ("FLTK", pronounced "fulltick")'.

entry.title: Cygwin — sig win
entry.summary: Cygwin is pronounced "sig win" (/ˈsɪɡwɪn/). POSIX compatibility layer for Windows (Cygnus + Windows); Wikipedia gives /ˈsɪɡwɪn/ SIG-win, confirmed by a Cygwin developer on the project mailing list.

entry.title: Nagios — nah ghee ose
entry.summary: Nagios is pronounced "nah ghee ose" (/ˈnɑːɡiːoʊs/). Veteran open-source infrastructure monitoring system (NetSaint 1999, renamed 2002); creator Ethan Galstad's official FAQ spells it out as "nah-ghee-ose" — "Nah" plus the start of "geese" plus the end of "verbose" — so the g is hard, never "NAY-jee-os", and Wikipedia records the same /ˈnɑːɡiːoʊs/.

entry.title: persona — per soh nuh
entry.summary: persona is pronounced "per soh nuh" (/pɚˈsoʊnə/). In agent and prompt design, a persona is the identity, role, tone, and behavioral frame assigned to an AI system. Stress the middle syllable: per-SOH-nuh, not PER-suh-nuh.

entry.title: affect — AFF ekt
entry.summary: affect is pronounced "AFF ekt" (/ˈæfɛkt/). In affective computing and psychology, the noun meaning observable emotion or feeling is AFF-ect, with first-syllable stress. The everyday verb meaning "influence" is uh-FECT; both established readings are included because the spelling is identical.

entry.title: affective — uh FEK tiv
entry.summary: affective is pronounced "uh FEK tiv" (/əˈfɛktɪv/). Affective computing and affective AI model emotion, mood, and emotionally responsive interaction. Say uh-FEK-tiv; it is often confused with "effective."

entry.title: anthropomorphism — an thruh puh MOR fiz um
entry.summary: anthropomorphism is pronounced "an thruh puh MOR fiz um" (/ˌænθrəpəˈmɔːrfɪzəm/). The attribution of human traits, intentions, or feelings to an AI agent or other nonhuman system. Six syllables, with primary stress on MOR: an-thruh-puh-MOR-fiz-um.

entry.title: prosody — PRAH suh dee
entry.summary: prosody is pronounced "PRAH suh dee" (/ˈprɑːsədi/). The rhythm, stress, pitch, and intonation of speech; a key signal for speech-emotion recognition and expressive voice models. PRAH-suh-dee is primary; a voiced-s PRAH-zuh-dee variant is also documented.

entry.title: valence — vay luns
entry.summary: valence is pronounced "vay luns" (/ˈveɪləns/). In emotion models, valence is the positive-to-negative dimension of affect, often paired with arousal. Say VAY-luhns, not VAL-ence.

entry.title: arousal — uh rouse uhl
entry.summary: arousal is pronounced "uh rouse uhl" (/əˈraʊzəl/). In affective computing, arousal measures emotional activation or intensity independently of positive or negative valence. Stress ROUSE: uh-ROUSE-uhl.

entry.title: interoception — in ter oh SEP shun
entry.summary: interoception is pronounced "in ter oh SEP shun" (/ˌɪntəroʊˈsɛpʃən/). The sensing of internal bodily signals such as heartbeat, breathing, and hunger; increasingly used in embodied-agent and computational-emotion models. Say in-ter-oh-SEP-shun.

entry.title: alexithymia — uh lek sih THIGH mee uh
entry.summary: alexithymia is pronounced "uh lek sih THIGH mee uh" (/əˌlɛksɪˈθaɪmiə/). Difficulty identifying or describing emotions, used in affect-recognition research and human-AI evaluation. Primary stress lands on THIGH: uh-lek-sih-THIGH-mee-uh.

entry.title: affordance — uh FOR dunce
entry.summary: affordance is pronounced "uh FOR dunce" (/əˈfɔːrdəns/). An action possibility offered by an environment to an agent; central to robotics, embodied AI, and action-aware world models. Stress FOR: uh-FOR-duhns.

entry.title: homeostasis — hoh mee oh STAY sis
entry.summary: homeostasis is pronounced "hoh mee oh STAY sis" (/ˌhoʊmioʊˈsteɪsɪs/). The regulation of internal stability; a useful framing for agents that model needs, drives, affect, and bodily state. Five syllables, with primary stress on STAY: hoh-mee-oh-STAY-sis.

entry.title: enactivism — ih NAK tih viz um
entry.summary: enactivism is pronounced "ih NAK tih viz um" (/ɪˈnæktɪvɪzəm/). A cognitive-science view in which cognition emerges through an agent's embodied interaction with its environment rather than passive representation alone. Say ih-NAK-tiv-iz-um.

entry.title: autopoiesis — aw toh poy EE sis
entry.summary: autopoiesis is pronounced "aw toh poy EE sis" (/ˌɔːtoʊpɔɪˈiːsɪs/). Self-production or self-maintenance in living systems, closely tied to enactive cognition and autonomous-agent theory. The final three syllables are poy-EE-sis, with primary stress on EE.

entry.title: Genie 3 — jee nee three
entry.summary: Genie 3 is pronounced "jee nee three" (/ˈdʒiːni ˈθriː/). Google DeepMind's real-time interactive world model, announced in 2025 and opened through Project Genie in 2026. The name is the ordinary word "genie" followed by the numeral: JEE-nee three.

entry.title: Marble — mar bul
entry.summary: Marble is pronounced "mar bul" (/ˈmɑːrbəl/). World Labs' multimodal model for creating editable, explorable 3D worlds from text, images, video, or layouts. Say MAR-buhl, like the ordinary English word.
